correctness.rationale: The balance equations yield S_i=1-(1+a/b)I_i and P_i=I_i. Differentiation shows f/Q strictly decreasing, proving symmetric uniqueness when R0>1 and nonexistence at R0<=1. The full physical 3n Jacobian is block diagonalized by common and transverse pathogen modes with nonnegative feedback gains. Each cubic has strictly positive coefficients and A1*A2-A3=(b+u)[u(a+b)+c(b+u+c)]+c*v*(u+c)>0. Strict cubic Hurwitz yields local exponential stability. The exact-rational Python-3 verifier built from this package returned VERIFY_OK for 2916 representative cases; universality comes from symbolic signs, not the tests.

originality.rationale: The source model establishes coexistence stability for no spillover and labels the positive-spillover stability statements conjectural. The present all-n exchangeable theorem proves those conjectured implications in the natural equal-parameter sector and extends them to arbitrary finite pathogen count. General symmetry reductions are antecedents; no checked full-text prior establishes the positive all-mode cubic for the lagged behavioral SIRS product incidence. Unindexed and full-text-access risks remain.
residual_risks: The published 2014 symmetry methods could contain broader transfer principles not captured by a claim-specific literature search; they are cited as antecedents, not ignored.
The full text of Berry et al. (2025) could not be inspected, so only its abstract and model description were compared; potential general-method overlap remains.
Unindexed or subsequently revised work may contain an equivalent all-n theorem.
The theorem does not extend automatically to heterogeneous pathogens or non-complete behavioral coupling.

value.rationale: Delayed behavior-mediated suppression in simultaneous epidemics has a concrete unresolved coexistence-stability question in the motivating research. The result classifies the exact positive coexistence equilibrium and excludes local Hopf instability across every finite pathogen count, all spillover strengths, all feedback sensitivities and all finite perception delays under exchangeable rates. Its structural certificate explains why a large information lag alone cannot destabilize this equilibrium, while avoiding unsupported global claims.
